sections.title: The Nature of Spiritual Warfare
observations: In this section, Paul addresses the nature of the conflict he faces, emphasizing that it is not against flesh and blood but against spiritual forces. He contrasts the weapons of the world with the spiritual weapons that God provides, which are powerful for tearing down strongholds.

Paul's use of the term 'strongholds' refers to arguments and pretensions that set themselves up against the knowledge of God. This highlights the importance of discerning truth from falsehood in the life of a believer.

sections.title: Paul's Authority and Apostolic Credentials
observations: Paul defends his authority as an apostle, which some in Corinth were questioning. He asserts that his authority comes from Christ and is not based on worldly standards or appearances.
This section emphasizes the importance of recognizing true authority in the church and the dangers of relying on superficial judgments.

sections.title: Boasting in the Lord
observations: Paul discusses the concept of boasting, stating that he will only boast in the Lord. He contrasts his ministry with those who boast in their own accomplishments or credentials.
This serves as a reminder for believers to focus on God's work in their lives rather than their own achievements.

importantVerses.commentary: For though we live in the world, we do not wage war as the world does. This verse encapsulates the essence of spiritual warfare, reminding believers that their struggles are not against physical enemies but against spiritual forces.
But, 'Let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.' This verse emphasizes the importance of humility and recognizing that any success in ministry comes from God alone.

questions: What does it mean to wage spiritual warfare in a practical sense for believers today?
How can we discern between true and false authority in the church?
In what ways can we ensure that our boasting is centered on the Lord rather than ourselves?
